model: Regulated utility FCFE at cost of equity (rate-base reinvestment, engine route; net debt zero)

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 313,625,618 common shares on issue at 2026-10-12 (Q3-2026 10-Q cover) plus ~0.3m dilutive nonvested awards and contingently convertible shares (Q3-2026 EPS note, 9M diluted add-back 0.5m). Held FLAT: future equity issuance (the $3bn ATM/forward programme) is netted out of the FCFE flows as a cash inflow from new holders, so diluting the count as well would charge it twice.
inputs.debt_memo: Not deducted (flows are post-interest). For the record at 2026-09-30: long-term debt 18,743 + current portion of LTD and finance leases 1,258 + non-current finance leases 206 = 20,207; unrestricted cash 451 (plus 102 restricted, 26 held for sale); preferred stock 224 (CMS Series C) + 37 (Consumers $4.50); NCI 569.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K Note 12 'Compensation expense recognized' $25m (CMS consolidated); shares withheld for award taxes $13m (statement of changes in equity, 'Common stock repurchased', 181k shares). No combined company figure, so the two are summed for sbc_incl_equity_taxes.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-06T21:00:02Z regular close (Yahoo chart API regularMarketTime 1793998802); not an after-hours print
inputs.wacc_rationale: The discount rate is a COST OF EQUITY, not a WACC, because the flow is to equity (post-interest, post-preferred, post-NCI). USD build: 10-year UST 4.86% (Yahoo ^TNX, 2026-11-06 close); regulated-utility equity beta ~0.55; ERP 5.0% -> CAPM 7.6%, rounded to 7.5% and held identical across all three scenarios (risk charged once, through the paths and weights). Matches the AEE build of the same date for cross-ticker comparability. For reference: allowed ROE 9.8-9.9% is a regulatory book return, not a market discount rate; CMS's dividend yield (3.3%) plus 6-8% growth implies the market is using ~9.5-11% on management's numbers or ~7% if growth halves.
inputs.lease_treatment: Finance leases ($212m) and operating leases are immaterial; lease cost is inside O&M and therefore inside pre-tax income. lease_cost_pct_path = 0; no lease liability in a (zero) net-debt bridge. One treatment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are ATTRIBUTABLE to common: pre-tax income is built net of preferred dividends and of the NCI share (largely HLBV allocations to NorthStar tax-equity investors), so neither the $261m of preferred nor the $569m NCI is deducted again in the bridge -- charged once. Quality-of-earnings caveat: 9M-2026 NCI losses ex-impairment were $199m (HLBV tax-equity accounting), which lifts attributable EPS without cash; the FCFE line (dividends - issuance) is unaffected, but the terminal value capitalises an earnings base that includes it.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE. dcf-methods SKILL.md has no regulated-utility row. The operating-company row would send CMS to the firm-level owner-FCF DCF, which is unusable here for the reason documented on AIA.NZ and in every utility build in this folder (AEE, ED, AEP, ETR, EVRG): reported FCF (OCF - capex) was -$1,589m in FY2025 and stays negative through the $25.8bn 2026-2030 plan by design; every dollar enters rate base and earns an allowed return (ROE 9.8-9.9%). A trial unlevered build at a ~6.25% WACC (EBITDA margin rising 35% -> 42.5% with rate base, capex gliding from 58% of revenue to a terminal 30%, cash tax 12% -> 22%) gave an enterprise value of ~$10bn against $20bn of net debt -- negative equity for a company earning ~12% ROE -- because book return on invested capital (~5.5%) sits below a market WACC while equity earns the allowed ROE through embedded cheap debt, ADIT and regulatory leverage. The economics are those of a compounder of book: value = PV of (net income - equity reinvested in rate-base growth) at the cost of equity = FCFE = dividends - net equity issuance. Run on the Drivers/engine route in the AEE/ED pattern so the dashboard reproduces it. ENGINE MAPPING (read the sliders with this key): 'revenue' = total operating revenue; 'EBITDA margin' = PRE-TAX INCOME ATTRIBUTABLE TO COMMON (after interest, preferred dividends and NCI) + SBC, as % of revenue -- it is NOT EBITDA (FY2025 operating EBITDA margin was 35.5%; the engine-equivalent was 15.8%); SBC path 0.30% so 'EBIT' = pre-tax attributable income; D&A and lease paths 0 (already inside pre-tax income); cash_tax_rate_path = effective book tax rate (19% -> 21%; under cost-of-service ratemaking cash-tax deferrals reduce rate base and accrue to customers, so the near-zero cash taxes CMS pays are deliberately not projected), so 'NOPAT' = net income available to common; 'capex' = equity reinvestment = increase in common equity (retained earnings + new common issued); working capital 0; FCF = FCFE. Net debt 0. NORMALISATION: FY2026 Y1 is ADJUSTED net income (guidance $3.83-3.90 raised/reaffirmed in the Q3-2026 release, base $3.88 x ~311m weighted shares = $1,207m), NOT trailing GAAP. GAAP 9M-2026 NI to common was $576m vs $775m because of the one-time NorthStar Clean Energy impairment, disposal and exit costs ($525m operating + $33m equity-method impairment, $102m of it borne by NCI; Q3 consolidated net loss $(91)m, attributable $123m, diluted EPS $0.39). Those charges are mostly non-cash write-downs on held-for-sale disposal groups ($826m assets / $101m liabilities held for sale at 2026-09-30) and are excluded; the expected sale proceeds are not added to a bridge either, and the divested projects' earnings are small enough that their loss is inside the guidance range. GUIDANCE ANCHORS: FY2026 adj EPS $3.83-3.90; FY2027 $4.08-4.17; long-term 6-8% adj EPS growth; capex $4.4bn 2026, $25.8bn 2026-2030 ($24.1bn Consumers); rate base growth >10%/yr; $3bn equity programme (May 2026) after $525m issued in FY2025 and $530m in 9M-2026; DPS $2.28 annualised (Q3-2026 $0.57). BASE SCHEDULE ($m): EPS 3.88, 4.12, then +6.5% (low-mid of 6-8%) 2028-2030, 6.0/5.5/5.0/4.5/4.0% 2031-35; weighted shares 311 -> 355 as $700/700/750/700/600/400/200m of equity is issued 2026-2032; NI 1,207, 1,323, 1,449, 1,583, 1,728, 1,864, 1,977, 2,077, 2,169, 2,258; dividends 709, 780, 851, 932, 1,017, 1,094 (DPS +6.5%/yr, ~59% payout) then payout 62/65/68/70% 2032-35; FCFE 9, 80, 101, 232, 417, 694, 1,026, 1,350, 1,475, 1,581. Implied ROE ~12-13% on book (FY2025 actual ~12%), terminal reinvestment 30% of NI vs g/ROE = 3/11.6 = 26%. SANITY: FY2026 NI 1,207 on revenue ~9,110 (9M-2026 revenue 6,742, +6.9% YoY). Firm owner-FCF CAGRs are undefined (negative in every year since FY2018); historical_growth.fcf_* are null for that reason. Buybacks: none (net issuer; buyback_cash 0 -- the $13m of withheld award shares is counted in sbc_incl_equity_taxes). last_fcf 115 = FY2025 FCFE = common dividends 653 - common issued 525 - award-tax withholding 13; reported_fcf 153 is the same flow with SBC and withholding added back (street basis). It is NOT OCF - capex (-1,589, carried in reported_fcf_firm_ocf_less_capex), which is not the flow this model values.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: management long-term adjusted EPS growth target 6-8% (low-mid used); equity CAGR rejected as the selector because it is inflated by ~$0.3-0.5bn/yr of new common issuance
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 9.8% vs revenue 5yr 5.9% and EPS 5yr 5.9% (divergence >30%): book equity is growing on new share issuance funding the capital plan, not only retained earnings. FY2021 EPS $4.66 includes the EnerBank sale gain; FY2022-25 revenue is flat because FY2022 carried high gas/fuel pass-through.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue FY2020 6,418 -> FY2025 8,539; FY2022 8,596. Diluted EPS FY2020 2.65, FY2022 2.85, FY2025 3.53. Total equity FY2020 6,077, FY2022 7,595, FY2025 9,711. Firm FCF (OCF - capex) negative every year since FY2018 (FY2025 -1,589) -- the capex supercycle, not distress. FCFE (dividends - net issuance) FY2025 +115.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +6.7%: 9M-2026 revenue +6.9% (6,742 vs 6,306) with the gas order ($139m, 9.80% ROE) effective Nov-2026. 2027-2029 +6.5%: ~10% rate-base growth lifts the non-fuel revenue requirement ~8%/yr while fuel/purchased-power pass-through (~38% of revenue) grows ~3%; the pending electric case ($468m ask, 10.25% ROE) lands in 2027. Fades to 3.5% by 2035 as the capital plan normalises. Revenue is only the scaling line here; value is set by the NI and reinvestment paths.
base.margin_rationale: NOT EBITDA: pre-tax income attributable to common / revenue, plus the 0.30% SBC line. Back-solved from the base NI schedule in inputs.notes at the tax path below (FY2025 actual 15.5% = 1,061 / (1 - 19.7%) / 8,539). Rises because the return-on-rate-base component outgrows pass-through revenue.
base.capex_rationale: Equity reinvestment = NI - FCFE = retained earnings + net new common, as % of revenue. 2026-2032 includes $700/700/750/700/600/400/200m of issuance from the $3bn programme; after 2032 growth is funded by retention as payout rises to 70%.
base.tax_rationale: Book effective rate (FY2025 19.7%; PTC/ITC benefits and excess-ADIT amortisation), drifting to 21% as wind/solar credits phase down under the 2025 tax law. NI is back-solved, so this only splits pre-tax from post-tax.
base.terminal_rationale: g 3.0%: inflation-plus rate-base growth after 2035 (load growth from electrification/data centres offset by the end of the coal-to-renewables build). Gordon at 7.5%/3.0% = 22.9x terminal FCFE (~16x terminal earnings at 70% payout), below the 30x cap, which is set at ~sector-median 16-17x P/E-equivalent; the tech 20x-FCF default would be ~14x P/E and bind in the bull case.
base.narrative: Management delivers guidance at the midpoint and the LOW-MID of the 6-8% algorithm (6.5%) through 2030 while issuing ~$3.5bn of equity: electric and gas cases keep being granted at ~60% of the ask with ROEs at 9.8-9.9%, the NorthStar exit closes by mid-2027 near carrying value, Campbell's DOE-order costs are recovered through FERC, and the 1 GW data-centre contract energises without the 9 GW pipeline adding to the plan. Moody's negative outlook resolves without a downgrade.

bull.margin_rationale: Back-solved from EPS 3.90 (top of FY2026 range), 4.17 (top of FY2027), +8% (top of the algorithm) 2028-2031, then 7/6/5/4.5%; weighted shares 311 -> 363 on $700/800/900/800/700/500/300m of issuance; NI 1,213 -> 2,561 by 2035.
bull.narrative: Large load is real: the 1 GW data-centre agreement is followed by further contracts out of the ~9 GW interconnection pipeline under the large-load tariff, adding rate base above the $25.8bn plan (and the September 2026 IRP's 19 GW / two gas plants come in on schedule), so EPS compounds at the top of 6-8%. The NorthStar exit removes impairment risk and simplifies the equity story; the 2026 electric case lands near the 10.25% ask; Moody's moves back to stable. Terminal growth 3.5% reflects a longer electrification runway.

bear.margin_rationale: Back-solved from EPS 3.83 (bottom of FY2026), 3.98 (below the FY2027 floor of 4.08), +4.5%/yr 2028-2030, then 4/3.5/3/3/2.5%; weighted shares 311 -> 375 because more equity ($700/900/900/800/600/400/200m) is issued at ~$62-71; NI 1,191 -> 1,992 by 2035.
bear.narrative: Michigan affordability politics bite: the 2026 electric case is granted at well under half the $468m ask with a sub-9.8% ROE (the 2025 gas case already came in at $139m vs $232m), regulatory lag widens on a rate base growing >10%/yr, and DOE keeps J.H. Campbell running with FERC cost recovery delayed. Moody's downgrades Consumers on the capital plan, lifting financing costs and forcing more equity at lower prices; NorthStar disposals realise below carrying value; the data-centre pipeline slips. EPS growth runs ~4.5% and misses the 2027 range.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance met at the midpoint, then EPS +6.5%/yr (low-mid of the 6-8% algorithm) on ~10% rate-base growth funded by ~$3.5bn of new equity through 2032. Rate cases keep landing at ~60% of the ask with 9.8-9.9% ROEs; the NorthStar exit closes near carrying value by mid-2027; Campbell costs are recovered at FERC; Moody's outlook stabilises without a downgrade.
scenario_narratives.bull: Large-load demand converts: beyond the signed 1 GW data-centre contract, more of the ~9 GW pipeline signs under the large-load tariff, lifting the capital plan and EPS growth to the top of 6-8%. The 2026 electric case lands near the 10.25% ask, the NorthStar exit removes the last non-utility volatility, and the credit outlook returns to stable.
scenario_narratives.bear: The regulatory axis breaks against CMS: the electric case is cut hard, ROEs slip below 9.8%, lag widens on a >10%/yr rate base, Campbell's DOE-order costs stay unrecovered, and a Moody's downgrade forces more equity at lower prices. EPS growth falls to ~4.5% and the stock re-rates as a slower bond proxy (terminal growth 2.5%).

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: CMS is a single-regulator (MPSC) business whose last gas order came in at 60% of the ask, Moody's has a negative outlook on Consumers tied to the capital plan, and the plan depends on continuous equity issuance. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs the data-centre pipeline to convert AND constructive orders AND a stable credit outlook at once. Base 50%: guidance has been met or raised for two decades and the 2026/2027 ranges were reaffirmed through the NorthStar charge.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A regulated utility is a compounder of book equity: value is the cash it returns to shareholders (dividends) net of the equity they must put back in (new issuance) to fund rate-base growth, discounted at the cost of equity. Firm-level FCF is structurally negative in a capex supercycle and is not a signal. The run-rate base is management's adjusted EPS guidance, which excludes the one-off NorthStar divestment charges that depress trailing GAAP earnings.
key_risks_to_valuation: Cost of equity: at 7.5% the base case is ~16x terminal earnings; every 50bp on the discount rate moves value ~10-15% (interest-rate / bond-proxy risk).
Rate-case outcomes at the MPSC (pending $468m electric case at 10.25% ROE ask; gas case granted $139m of $232m).
Equity issuance price: issuance is charged at face, so issuing well below intrinsic value would dilute more than modelled; issuing above it would be accretive (not credited).
Credit: Moody's negative outlook on Consumers; a downgrade raises financing costs and equity needs.

Earnings quality: HLBV tax-equity NCI allocations (~$200m+ in 9M-2026) and pension/AFUDC other income lift adjusted EPS without equivalent cash; the FCFE line is cash, but the terminal value capitalises reported earnings.
NorthStar divestment proceeds and J.H. Campbell DOE-order cost recovery.
